claims.claim: Procopius of Gaza was a Christian sophist and rhetorician, one of the most important representatives of the Rhetorical School of Gaza.
Procopius of Gaza was born c. 465 and died c. 528.
Procopius of Gaza was perhaps the foremost figure of the 'School of Gaza', a group of Christian rhetoricians of the 5th–6th century.
Procopius of Gaza was born c. 475 and died c. 538 according to some sources.
Procopius of Gaza was born in Gaza c. 475 and died in Gaza c. 528.
Procopius of Gaza lived during the time of Justin and Justinian (518–565).
Procopius of Gaza was the preceptor of Choricius the sophist.
Procopius of Gaza's colleagues at the School of Gaza included Choricius, Aeneas, and his brother Zacharias.
A collection of 165 letters by Procopius of Gaza has survived, addressed to persons of rank, friends, and literary opponents.
The letter collection of Procopius of Gaza includes 169 letters by Procopius's hand preserved together with an additional five to him from his addressee Megethius.
The recipients of Procopius of Gaza's letters include friends, relatives, colleagues, fellow students, other sophists, and pupils.
The letters of Procopius of Gaza contain advice, requests for favors and recommendations.
